pages.textMedium:
Far out in the deep blue sea lived the White Whale. He was the toughest whale in the whole ocean. He wasn't scared of sharks. He wasn't scared of storms.

He had only one problem: he was curious. Way too curious. If something went blip, he had to go and poke it with his nose.
pages.textLong:
Far out in the deep blue sea lived the White Whale. He was the toughest whale in the whole ocean. He wasn't scared of sharks. He wasn't scared of storms.

He had only one problem: he was curious. Way too curious. If something went blip, he had to go and poke it with his nose.

pages.textMedium:
One night he spotted a red light, far, far away. It glowed at the bottom of the sea like a tiny campfire.

"What is THAT?" said the White Whale. "I'll just take a quick look."

Remember that. A quick look. Ha.
pages.textLong:
One night he spotted a red light, far, far away. It glowed at the bottom of the sea like a tiny campfire.

"What is THAT?" said the White Whale. "I'll just take a quick look."

Remember that. A quick look. Ha.

On the way he passed an old anchor. He poked it. BONG. He passed a rusty bucket. He poked it. Clonk.

Then a whole school of tiny fish came the other way. They had lined up in the shape of an arrow. The arrow pointed away from the red light.

"Nice arrow," said the White Whale, and swam on.
pages.scene: Night sea, dark blue. The White Whale swims to the right and pokes a big rusty anchor half buried in the sand with his nose; wobble lines ring out from the anchor. Above him a school of tiny silver fish has lined up in the shape of an arrow pointing left, away from the red glow, which is a little bigger now on the right. A dented rusty bucket rolls on the sea floor behind him.

pages.textMedium:
He swam and he swam. The red light got bigger. The water got warmer. First it was warm like a bath. Then it was warm like soup.

A little fish zoomed past the other way, shouting, "Wrong way, big guy!"

The White Whale did not listen. Tough whales never do.
pages.textLong:
He swam and he swam. The red light got bigger. The water got warmer. First it was warm like a bath. Then it was warm like soup.

A little fish zoomed past the other way, shouting, "Wrong way, big guy!"

The White Whale did not listen. Tough whales never do.

pages.textMedium:
At the foot of a mountain sat a crab, fanning himself with one claw. The seaweed around him hung limp, like boiled spaghetti.

"Don't," said the crab.

"Don't what?" said the White Whale.

"Whatever you're about to do."

Did he listen? You already know. That was warning number two. He was collecting them.
pages.textLong:
At the foot of a mountain sat a crab, fanning himself with one claw. The seaweed around him hung limp, like boiled spaghetti.

"Don't," said the crab.

"Don't what?" said the White Whale.

"Whatever you're about to do."

Did he listen? You already know. That was warning number three. He was collecting them.
pages.scene: The foot of the dark underwater mountain, the water warm orange. The red crab sits on his rock, fanning himself with one claw and holding the other up like a stop sign, grumpy and sweating. The White Whale leans in close, cheerful, clearly not listening. The seaweed droops limp like cooked spaghetti. The small blue-shelled snail nearby has one sweat drop on its forehead.

pages.textMedium:
The light came out of a hole in the side of the mountain. A round, dark hole, exactly one whale wide.

Would you swim into a hole like that? No. You're smart.

"Perfect fit," said the White Whale. And in he went, nose first. The crab just shook his head.
pages.textLong:
The light came out of a hole in the side of the mountain. A round, dark hole, exactly one whale wide.

Would you swim into a hole like that? No. You're smart.

"Perfect fit," said the White Whale. And in he went, nose first. The crab just shook his head.

pages.textMedium:
In went his nose. No problem. In went his flippers. No problem. In went his big round belly — problem.

He wiggled. He waggled. He pushed and he puffed. Nothing. The toughest whale in the ocean was stuck like a cork in a bottle.
pages.textLong:
In went his nose. No problem. In went his flippers. No problem. In went his big round belly — problem.

He wiggled. He waggled. He pushed and he puffed. Nothing. The toughest whale in the ocean was stuck like a cork in a bottle.

pages.textMedium:
"Hold still," sighed the crab. He grabbed the whale's tail with both claws. The little fish grabbed the crab. The snail grabbed the little fish.

"One, two, three — PULL!"

They pulled until the crab's eyes nearly popped off their stalks. Did the whale move? Not one tiny bit. But the snail got a bit longer.
pages.textLong:
"Hold still," sighed the crab. He grabbed the whale's tail with both claws. The little fish grabbed the crab. The snail grabbed the little fish.

"One, two, three — PULL!"

They pulled until the crab's eyes nearly popped off their stalks. Did the whale move? Not one tiny bit. But the snail got a bit longer.
pages.scene: Outside the mountain: a pulling chain. The crab grips the White Whale's tail with both claws, the little teal fish pulls the crab by a back leg with its mouth, and the blue-shelled snail holds the fish's tail fin, stretched long like a rubber band. Everyone strains with puffed cheeks. The whale's back half sticks out of the hole and has not moved at all.

pages.textLong:
Then the snail had an idea. Snails are slippery. So he crawled all the way around the whale's belly and left a shiny trail of slime.

It took one hour. It tickled like crazy.

"Now try," said the snail.

The White Whale pushed. He slid forward the length of one snail. And then he was stuck again. Tighter.
pages.scene: Close on the rim of the hole where the rock squeezes the White Whale's belly. The blue-shelled snail crawls along the rim around the belly, very proud, leaving a glittering silver slime trail. The whale's tail is curled up tight because it tickles. The crab watches with his claws on his hips; the little fish has fallen asleep waiting, a tiny bubble at its mouth.

pages.textMedium:
The crab sat down. "Well," he said, "you live here now. I'll bring you a sandwich on Thursdays."

Inside the tunnel, where nobody could see, the whale's lip wobbled. The toughest whale in the ocean, with his bottom sticking out of a mountain. For ever.

"No," he said. "One more push. A really big one."
pages.textLong:
The crab sat down. "Well," he said, "you live here now. I'll bring you a sandwich on Thursdays."

Inside the tunnel, where nobody could see, the whale's lip wobbled. The toughest whale in the ocean, with his bottom sticking out of a mountain. For ever.

"No," he said. "One more push. A really big one."
pages.scene: Outside the mountain, quiet and a bit sad. The White Whale's back half hangs out of the hole, tail drooping limp. The crab sits on his rock and shrugs with both claws. The little fish gently pats the whale's tail with a fin. The snail has stuck a small starfish on the whale's tail like a decoration, to make it look like home.

pages.textMedium:
He took the deepest breath of his life and pushed. The rock squeezed his belly. Squeeeeze. And deep down inside, something started to rumble. Grumble-bumble.

"Oh no," whispered the White Whale. "Not now. Please not now."

But it was now.
pages.textLong:
He took the deepest breath of his life and pushed. The rock squeezed his belly. Squeeeeze. And deep down inside, something started to rumble. Grumble-bumble.

"Oh no," whispered the White Whale. "Not now. Please not now."

Outside, the crab felt the rock tremble under his feet. The snail pressed one ear to the whale. (Do snails have ears? This one did.)

Grumble-bumble. GRUMBLE-BUMBLE.

"Is that thunder?" asked the little fish.

"That," said the crab, "is not thunder. Everybody behind the rock. NOW."
pages.scene: Outside the mountain. Rumble lines shake the rock around the hole and the White Whale's tail sticks out stiff as a board. The crab, eyes wide, points urgently with one claw to the back of his rock, legs wobbling. The snail is stuck to the whale's side, listening, eye-stalks pressed flat. The little fish looks up for a thunderstorm that is not there. Pebbles hop on the sea floor.

pages.textMedium:
PRRRRRRRT!

It was the biggest fart in the history of the sea. It roared like a rocket engine. WHOOSH! The White Whale shot through the hole like a white torpedo and popped out on the other side.

Stuck? Not anymore.
pages.textLong:
PRRRRRRRT!

It was the biggest fart in the history of the sea. It roared like a rocket engine. WHOOSH! The White Whale shot through the hole like a white torpedo and popped out on the other side.

Stuck? Not anymore.

pages.textMedium:
Outside, things were not so good. The crab went head over heels, three times, and landed upside down in the seaweed. The little fish turned green.

And the snail? He flew further in two seconds than he had travelled in his whole life.

"Again!" said the snail.

"Never again," said the crab, holding his nose.
pages.textLong:
The crab had peeked out from behind his rock. He should not have peeked. He went head over heels, three times, and landed upside down in the seaweed. The little fish turned green.

And the snail? He flew further in two seconds than he had travelled in his whole life.

"Again!" said the snail.

"Never again," said the crab, holding his nose.
pages.scene: Outside the mountain just after the blast. A big green-yellow cloud of bubbles drifts out of the now empty, glowing hole. The crab hangs upside down, tangled in seaweed, pinching his nose with one claw. The little teal fish has gone green in the face. The blue-shelled snail sails through the water shell first, spinning, with a huge delighted grin.

pages.textLong:
And where was he? Inside a volcano. A real one, as tall as a tower. Far below, lava glowed and bubbled. Blop. Blop. The water was hot like tea.

He looked back at the tunnel. No, thank you. He looked up. Way, way up at the top was a tiny round hole, full of stars.

"Hm," said the White Whale.
pages.scene: Inside the volcano, seen from low down so the chamber looks as tall as a tower. The White Whale, small in the middle of the hot orange water, tips his head back and stares up at a tiny round opening full of night sky and stars far above. Lava glows at the very bottom. Behind him the tunnel mouth lets out a last wisp of green bubbles. The two shy round eyes from the tunnel peek out of a crack in the wall.

pages.textLong:
A big bubble rose up from the lava, right in front of him. It was round. It was orange. It went blip.

And you know what happens when something goes blip.

He poked it with his nose. POP! A puff of black smoke hit him right in the face. It smelled of burnt toast and old socks.
pages.scene: Inside the volcano. The White Whale has just popped a glowing orange bubble with his nose: a black puff of smoke sits on his face, his nose is sooty and his eyes blink in surprise. More orange bubbles drift up around him through the hot water. The lava stays far below. The pink shrimp from the tunnel watches from a ledge with both feelers over its eyes.

pages.textMedium:
And where was he? Inside a volcano. A real one. Far below, lava glowed and bubbled. Blop. Blop. Way up at the top was a tiny round hole, full of stars. The water was hot. And the smell! Smoke and burnt toast.

It crept up his nose. It tickled. Tickle, tickle, tickle...
pages.textLong:
The smoke crept up his nose. It tickled. Tickle, tickle, tickle...

"Not a sneeze," said the White Whale. "Not in here."

Because a whale sneeze inside a volcano? Even he knew that was a bad idea.

Tickle. Tickle. TICKLE.

He held his nose shut with one flipper. He held his breath. He thought about boring things. Sand. Seaweed. More sand.

His face went from white to pink to purple.

Then he looked up at the tiny hole full of stars. He looked down at the lava. And the White Whale had an idea.

He let go of his nose.
pages.scene: Inside the volcano. The White Whale clamps one flipper over his nose, cheeks puffed out, his white face turned pink and purple. His eyes are rolled upward toward the tiny starry opening high above. Wisps of smoke curl around him. A thought bubble over his head shows a plain little heap of sand. The pink shrimp is already hiding behind a rock with only its feelers showing.

pages.textMedium:
He looked up at the stars. He looked down at the lava. "Fine," said the White Whale. "Up it is."

"Ah... ah... AH-CHOOOO!"

The sneeze spun the water round and round, faster and faster, until it was a whirling, twirling, red-hot LAVA TORNADO. Up went the tornado. Up went the White Whale, right in the middle of it.

Was he scared? "WHEEEEE!" Nope.
pages.textLong:
"Ah... ah... AH-CHOOOO!"

The sneeze spun the water round and round, faster and faster, until it was a whirling, twirling, red-hot LAVA TORNADO. Up went the tornado. Up went the White Whale, right in the middle of it.

Was he scared? "WHEEEEE!" Nope.

pages.textMedium:
POP! Out of the top of the mountain he flew, like a cork out of a bottle. Higher than the waves. Higher than the clouds. Past one very surprised seagull.

Far below, a crab, a snail and a little fish stuck their heads out of the water and stared.

"He's waving," said the snail.

He was.
pages.textLong:
POP! Out of the top of the mountain he flew, like a cork out of a bottle. Higher than the waves. Higher than the clouds. Past one very surprised seagull.

Far below, a crab, a snail and a little fish stuck their heads out of the water and stared.

He was.
pages.scene: Night sky above the volcano island. The White Whale is high in the air on top of a glowing orange fountain shooting out of the mountain top, waving one flipper, thrilled. Beside him a seagull hangs in mid-air with its beak wide open, dropping a feather. Down at the waterline three small heads poke out of the waves and stare up: the crab, the little fish, and the snail riding on the crab's head.

pages.textMedium:
SPLASH! Back into the cool, dark sea.

He floated on his back and looked at the stars. The seagull landed on his belly. He was too tired to poke it.

"Just a quick look," he yawned.

And then he fell asleep. Because even the toughest whale in the ocean has to sleep sometime.
